metadata.processing_notes: Comprehensive extraction from Colonial Office List 1905. Data extracted from 16 colony files with full detail preservation. Historical spelling and terminology preserved as per methodology. All numerical data, salaries, coordinates, and population figures extracted verbatim from source documents.

events.description: Antigua discovered by Columbus in 1493, who named it after a church in Seville, called Santa Maria La Antigua
First inhabited by a few English from St. Kitts in 1632
Charles II made a formal grant of the island to Lord Willoughby, who sent out a large number of colonists
Declared a British possession by the Treaty of Breda, 1666
Legislative Council passed an Act abrogating itself and substituting the Crown Colony system
St. Salvador, one of the islands composing the Bahamas chain, was the first land discovered by Columbus on his voyage in 1492
Settlers from the Bermudas found their way in considerable numbers to Eleuthera
Granted by Charles II to a proprietary body
Confirmed in British possession at the Peace of Versailles
Abolition of slavery, four years before the tax of 4½ per cent. duties was abolished by an Act of Parliament in 1838
The island suffered severely from the effects of a disastrous hurricane
Mosesh and his tribe appealed to be taken under the authority of the Queen, and Sir Philip Wodehouse received authority to recognise them as British subjects
Annexed to the Cape by Act of the Cape Legislature, No. 12 of 1871
Her Majesty's Government took steps for carrying on the government under the immediate authority of the Crown
British Protectorate proclaimed over Bechuanaland by Sir Charles Warren
Dr. Jameson's raid into the Transvaal, crossed the border with police, defeated by the Boers at Doornkop, surrendered on 2nd January 1896
Admiral Sir George Somers' ship, The Sea Venture, wrecked upon one of the reefs while conveying colonists to Virginia
Great earthquake engulfed Port Royal
Slave Trade abolished, there were 323,827 slaves in Jamaica
Abolition of slavery, Jamaica received 6,161,927£ of the 20,000,000£ granted by the Imperial Government as compensation to slave-owners
Serious rebellion among the black population suppressed by Governor Eyre with unnecessary violence
Grand Master Hompesch capitulated to Napoleon Bonaparte, who dispersed the Order of Knights of St. John
The government was placed in the hands of Great Britain after French surrender
Finally annexed to the British Crown by the Treaty of Paris
